task.description:
This is WF-03 Steps 0.5 (registry lookup) and 1 (diagnose) combined into one dispatch, per docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md. You are on branch fix/ISS-0451-persistent-poller-crash-budget-20260904 (already checked out and pushed by Step 00).

STEP 0.5: Search docs/issues/*.yaml for any resolved entry describing the same symptom class (a supervisor's restart-intensity budget being exhausted by a persistent/non-transient fault cascading to a parent). Note in your result whether a prior match exists, and if the same root cause has recurred before (which would raise severity to at least MAJOR regardless of the filed severity -- ISS-0451 is already filed MAJOR).

STEP 1: Reproduce ISS-0451 directly, don't diagnose from the issue's prose alone. The issue (docs/issues/ISS-0451.yaml, already filed) claims: Letflow.Supervisor (top-level, lib/letflow/application.ex) uses :one_for_one with the OTP DEFAULT restart intensity (3 restarts / 5 seconds, never overridden), and Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers has its own max_restarts: 5, max_seconds: 60. REQ-219's own test (test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs) only proves isolation for a SINGLE crash-loop-then-clear event -- the test clears its force-crash flag right after Pollers' first :DOWN, before the top-level supervisor's own restart of Pollers could re-trigger the same crash. Verify directly: (a) confirm the top-level Letflow.Supervisor's actual restart-intensity config in lib/letflow/application.ex (read it, don't take the issue's word for it), (b) confirm Pollers' actual max_restarts/max_seconds in lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers.ex, (c) work out and state the concrete restart-intensity arithmetic for what happens when a Poller fault is PERSISTENT (never cleared): how many times does Pollers itself have to exit-and-be-restarted-by-the-top-level before the top-level's own 3-in-5s budget is exhausted, and roughly how fast (in wall-clock seconds) would that actually happen given Pollers' own 60-second window, (d) if practical, write and run a throwaway probe (a small script or an iex -S mix session, NOT a permanent test file) that actually starts a minimal supervision tree shaped like this one with a poller that always crashes, and observes whether the top-level supervisor itself exits -- this is the kind of direct verification core-directives.md's 'No Speculation' and 'Re-derive under the conditions the property is actually about' sections require, not merely trusting the arithmetic. If you build a throwaway probe, put it in scratch/ (git-ignored) and do not commit it.

Do NOT implement the fix. Your job is root-cause diagnosis only, and to recommend a routing path: does this need a full CODE-DESIGNER pass (design an explicit fix: raise the top-level's restart intensity, and/or add a circuit-breaker/backoff to Pollers, per the issue's own two candidate options), or is there a smaller mechanical fix. Given AGENT_SYSTEM.md's roster, this DOES need CODE-DESIGNER -- ISS-0451's own acceptance criteria require a documented restart-intensity arithmetic decision (AC2), which is a design decision, not a mechanical patch -- but confirm this yourself rather than taking that as given, and state your reasoning.

Write the diagnosis into result.summary: root cause (not just symptom), the concrete arithmetic from (c), what a fix needs to change, and whether your Step 0.5 registry lookup found any prior match.
acceptance_criteria: result.summary states the top-level Letflow.Supervisor's actual restart-intensity value, quoted from the real file (not assumed to be the OTP default without checking)
result.summary states Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers' actual max_restarts/max_seconds value, quoted from the real file
result.summary contains the concrete restart-intensity arithmetic: how many Pollers-level budget-exhaustion cycles it takes to exhaust the top-level's budget, and the wall-clock timing reasoning
result.summary states whether a throwaway probe was run and, if so, what it observed (or explains why a probe was impractical and what evidence substitutes for it)
result.summary states the Step 0.5 registry-lookup outcome explicitly
next_action names the recommended next step (CODE-DESIGNER, with reasoning)

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): searched docs/issues/*.yaml (grep for restart-intensity/crash-loop/max_restarts terms) and found exactly two related entries, ISS-0425 and ISS-0421 -- both status: open (neither resolved), both the ARCHITECTURAL predecessor issues REQ-219 was built to close (flat supervision tree, default OTP restart intensity exposed to a crash-looping child). Neither is a resolved entry describing this exact residual gap, so this is NOT a recurrence of a previously-fixed-and-regressed issue -- it is the first diagnosis of a specific gap that REVIEWER identified while gating REQ-219 itself (handoffs/WF02-REQ219-20260903/step-02d-reviewer.json's own 'crash_cascade_finding_verdict', which explicitly recommended registering this as a new issue rather than blocking REQ-219's gate). Severity stays MAJOR as filed; no upgrade warranted since there is no prior 'resolved' entry for this exact root cause to have regressed from.

STEP 1 (diagnose):

(a) Top-level Letflow.Supervisor's actual restart-intensity config -- read lib/letflow/application.ex line 51 directly: `opts = [strategy: :one_for_one, name: Letflow.Supervisor]` passed to `Supervisor.start_link(children, opts)`. NO max_restarts/max_seconds key anywhere in that keyword list (confirmed by reading the whole file, 54 lines, in full -- not assumed). Per OTP's Supervisor documentation this defaults to max_restarts: 3, max_seconds: 5 -- the OTP default, never overridden, exactly as ISS-0451 claims.

(b) Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers' actual restart-intensity config -- read lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers.ex line 104 directly: `Supervisor.init(children, strategy: :one_for_one, max_restarts: 5, max_seconds: 60)`. Confirmed max_restarts: 5, max_seconds: 60, exactly as ISS-0451 claims and as the module's own moduledoc (lines 15-23) documents as a DELIBERATE override looser than the OTP default.

(c) Restart-intensity arithmetic for a PERSISTENT (never-clearing) Poller fault: Pollers' own budget (5 restarts/60s) bounds only restarts of the individual Poller GenServer WITHIN Pollers. Once that budget is exhausted, Pollers itself (the whole supervisor process) exits and is restarted BY THE TOP-LEVEL Letflow.Supervisor -- this is one restart against the top level's OWN 3-restarts/5-seconds budget. If the fault is persistent, the freshly-restarted Pollers immediately re-enters the identical crash-loop (same fault, nothing cleared it), exhausts its own 5/60 budget again, exits again -- a second top-level-budget restart. A third such cycle is the 3rd top-level restart; per OTP semantics the (max_restarts+1)-th restart attempt within the window triggers exhaustion, so on the 4th Pollers-level exit arriving within any rolling 5-second top-level window, Letflow.Supervisor's own budget is exhausted and IT exits too -- cascading to kill Letflow.Repo and Bandit (Infrastructure and Http), the exact incident REQ-219 exists to make impossible. So the answer to 'how many Pollers-level budget-exhaustion cycles' is: it takes only 3 additional Pollers-level exits after the first (i.e. the 4th time Pollers as a whole dies) to exhaust the top level's budget, PROVIDED those exits land inside a rolling 5-second window of each other. Wall-clock timing: each individual Poller crash-loop-to-Pollers-exhaustion cycle is FAST -- the Poller's own first tick is zero-delay (Process.send_after(self(), :tick, 0), confirmed in lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex and mirrored in the probe below), so 5 restarts happen in low tens-of-milliseconds, not anywhere near the 60-second window Pollers' own budget allows. Since one full Pollers-exhaustion-to-exit cycle takes on the order of 10-50ms (not 60s), FOUR such cycles comfortably land inside the top-level's 5-second window with enormous margin -- there is no scenario where the top-level's window would 'roll past' and reset before the cascade completes. This confirms REVIEWER's own finding in step-02d-reviewer.json verbatim, now with concrete measured numbers rather than reasoning alone.

(d) Throwaway probe WAS run (scratch/iss0451_probe.exs, standalone `elixir` script, no Mix.install/network dependency, git-ignored, not committed) -- built a minimal 3-level tree shaped exactly like the real one: Probe.TopSupervisor (:one_for_one, NO max_restarts/max_seconds override, copied by omission from application.ex) supervising Probe.Pollers (:one_for_one, max_restarts: 5, max_seconds: 60, copied verbatim from pollers.ex) supervising Probe.CrashyWorker (a GenServer whose init/1 returns {:ok, state} -- a genuine successful start, exactly like the real Poller -- then schedules a zero-delay :tick via Process.send_after(self(), :tick, 0), and whose handle_info(:tick, state) unconditionally raises, with NOTHING ever clearing the fault, unlike pollers_test.exs's own AC4 test which clears :force_poller_crash right after the first :DOWN). Ran on this project's actual pinned toolchain (Elixir 1.20.3 / OTP 29, confirmed via `elixir --version`). OBSERVED RESULT, read directly from the run (not inferred): Probe.TopSupervisor.init/1 ran 1 time; Probe.Pollers.init/1 ran 4 times (1 initial + 3 top-level-triggered restarts -- exactly the OTP default max_restarts: 3 budget being consumed and then exhausted on the 4th attempt); Probe.CrashyWorker.init/1 (and its tick-raise) fired 24 times total across those 4 Pollers incarnations (roughly 5-6 crashes per incarnation, consistent with Pollers' own max_restarts: 5 being exhausted each time); the driver process, monitoring Probe.TopSupervisor's own pid, received `{:DOWN, ref, :process, top_pid, :shutdown}` -- i.e. Probe.TopSupervisor itself exited. Total wall-clock from probe start to top-level exit: 96ms. This is direct, first-hand, empirical confirmation -- not merely arithmetic reasoning -- that a persistent inner-child fault cascades through both restart-intensity layers and takes down the top-level supervisor, well under 1 second, several orders of magnitude faster than Pollers' own 60-second window. (Iteration note: an earlier probe draft crashed the worker synchronously inside init/1 via {:stop, reason} -- this produced a supervisor START FAILURE, not a post-start crash, which fails differently in OTP (Supervisor.start_link/2 returns {:error, ...} synchronously without ever exercising the restart-intensity retry path) and would have been a probe of the wrong mechanism; corrected to a genuine post-start crash via handle_info before treating the result as evidence, per core-directives.md's 'Re-derive under the conditions the property is actually about.')

ROOT CAUSE (not just symptom): REQ-219's layering (Letflow.Supervisor -> {Infrastructure, Pollers, Http}) correctly isolates a SINGLE Pollers-level crash-loop-and-exit event -- the top-level's default 3/5s budget comfortably absorbs one such restart. The root cause of ISS-0451 is that the design left the top-level Letflow.Supervisor at the unmodified OTP default restart intensity, which was sized for a flat 20-child tree of independent, individually-unlikely-to-crash-loop infrastructure processes, not for a tree where one specific child (Pollers) is EXPECTED to occasionally exhaust ITS OWN, deliberately-loosened budget as designed behavior (pollers.ex's own moduledoc calls a full Pollers exit-and-restart 'this closes the documented, non-hypothetical incident' -- i.e. it is an anticipated, not merely possible, event). Nothing in REQ-219's design or acceptance criteria bounds how many TIMES that anticipated event can recur, and no backoff/circuit-breaker exists inside Pollers to make a persistent fault degrade to a stopped-but-not-repeatedly-crash-looping state. So a transient fault (the scenario REQ-219's own AC4 test constructs and asserts) is fully and correctly isolated; a persistent fault (a permanently misconfigured tenant schema, a permanently unreachable dependency queried every tick) is NOT bounded by anything in the current design, and empirically cascades to the top level in well under a second per the probe above.

WHY EXISTING TESTS DIDN'T CATCH IT: test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs's own AC4 test (the 'crash-loop isolation' describe block) is explicit about this in its own inline comment (lines 127-143) -- it deliberately clears :force_poller_crash and flips :start_scheduler back to false IMMEDIATELY after observing the first :DOWN from the manually-restarted Pollers pid, specifically to prevent the freshly-restarted Pollers from immediately re-crash-looping and taking the whole top-level supervisor down mid-test (the test's own comment calls this 'GENUINE TIMING HAZARD, found empirically while mutation-testing this test'). That is a correct and necessary test-hygiene choice for AC4 as REQ-219 actually scopes it (a SINGLE restart event, per decision 3's own text and AC4's own wording), but it structurally cannot exercise -- and does not claim to exercise -- what happens when nothing external clears the fault, which is exactly the scenario a persistent production fault presents.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS TO CHANGE: per ISS-0451's own two candidate options (neither prescribed) -- (a) raise the top-level Letflow.Supervisor's own restart intensity high enough to tolerate at least one full Pollers-budget-exhaustion cycle (or several) without exiting itself, and/or (b) give Pollers a circuit-breaker/backoff so a persistent fault degrades to a stopped-but-not-crash-looping state rather than repeatedly exhausting its own budget and forcing a top-level restart every time. Choosing between (or combining) these, and picking concrete numbers/mechanism, is a genuine design decision -- there is no single mechanically-obvious answer, and ISS-0451's own AC2 (per the issue queue's acceptance criteria referenced in this run) requires the restart-intensity arithmetic decision to be DOCUMENTED, which is design-artifact content (a moduledoc rationale, a chosen intensity value with justification), not a code patch alone.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design (WF-03 Step 2). Reasoning: this is not a mechanical/one-line fix for three reasons verified above, not merely asserted: (1) the fix requires CHOOSING a concrete restart-intensity value or backoff mechanism -- there is no single correct number derivable from the code alone, e.g. 'raise the top level to N restarts/M seconds' requires deciding N and M against a stated rationale, exactly the kind of judgment call CODE-DESIGNER's design-artifact process exists for (see lib/letflow/design/req219-supervision-layering.md itself as the precedent for how this project documents restart-intensity rationale); (2) ISS-0451's own filed scope explicitly offers two non-mechanical alternative directions (raise top-level intensity vs. add a circuit-breaker/backoff to Pollers) that trade off differently (a raised top-level intensity is simpler but still eventually exhausts under a truly permanent fault and also loosens the top level's protection against an unrelated infra crash-loop; a circuit-breaker changes Pollers' own behavior and needs its own state-shape/timeout design) -- selecting between them, or combining them, needs a design pass, not implementation discretion; (3) whichever direction is chosen needs new/updated acceptance-criteria-shaped documentation (a moduledoc rationale mirroring pollers.ex's own existing 'Restart intensity override -- DELIBERATE, not the OTP default' section) and, per WF-03 Step 4, a fail-then-pass regression test exercising a PERSISTENT (not self-clearing) fault -- designing that test mechanism (how to safely induce and then classify a persistent-fault cascade without actually taking down a real test run's Letflow.Repo, mirroring but extending pollers_test.exs's own careful AC4 test-hygiene handling) is itself a design decision requiring the same rigor req219-supervision-layering.md's own §4/§5 test-mechanism sections received. This is not merely 'given as true because the dispatch said so' -- confirmed independently by the reasoning above, matching the dispatch's own instruction to verify rather than take it as given.
